ledger.note: 18 December 1846: Britain takes Labuan. 'Brooke acquired the island for Britain through the Treaty of Labuan with the Sultan of Brunei, Omar Ali Saifuddin II on 18 December 1846'; Captain Rodney Mundy witnessed the accession on 24 December 1846.

1848: Labuan becomes a Crown colony. Infobox 'Establishment of the crown colony: 1848'; 'by 1848, the island was made a crown colony and free port with [Brooke] appointed as the first Governor' (infobox term 1848-1852). The event is a status caption, not a new name.

region.text: Labuan island with its six smaller islands (Burung, Daat, Kuraman, Papan, Rusukan Kecil, Rusukan Besar)

ledger.note: 1890: the North Borneo Company administers Labuan. 'From 1890, Labuan came to be administered by the North Borneo Chartered Company' (infobox 'Transferred to North Borneo: 1890'). Sovereignty stayed British; the british-north-borneo dossier records the same change as a gain.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch, from the colony-of-labuan suggestion in the se-02-c report. One page opened (two prompts). Unsettled: (1) the dossier ends in 1907 because the straits-settlements dossier already carries Labuan from 1 January 1907 (gain, Japanese occupation 1942-1945, loss to british-north-borneo in 1946); the report suggestion 1846-1946 is not followed to avoid drawing the island in two dossiers; the straits-settlements gain names british-colonial-empire as counterpart where it should name this dossier; (2) 1890-1904 is drawn in british-north-borneo as the Company's administration (gain from british-colonial-empire); the events here mirror it; (3) the page gives no area; (4) the Japanese renaming 'Maeda Island' (1942) and the surrender of 9-10 September 1945 are in the sibling dossiers; (5) the Brooke connection is Sarawak's (kingdom-of-sarawak); (6) capital coordinates approximate; (7) no governors strip: the page lists governors, only the first (Brooke, 1848-1852) and last were read.
